name: Autothermal reforming with CO2 capture (blue hydrogen)
applications: hydrogen for power and industry hubs
principle: Natural gas is partly combusted with oxygen from an air separation unit inside the reformer, which supplies the heat for steam reforming in the same vessel. Because there is no large fired furnace, almost all CO2 ends up in the high-pressure shifted syngas, where a solvent unit removes it at high capture rates. A small fired heater remains for preheating.

process_steps.name: Autothermal reforming
equipment: refractory-lined ATR reactor with burner and catalyst bed

advantages: Higher capture rate than SMR without a separate flue gas capture unit
Large single trains suit hydrogen hubs and blue ammonia
Slightly lower NETL cost than SMR with capture
limitations: Needs an air separation unit and its power
Residual emissions from the fired heater and upstream methane
Depends on CO2 transport and storage
